name: Acton
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Acton, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Acton, MA: the Journey to Bethlehem living nativity and a Holiday Craft Workshop at the Acton Recreation Center.
lede: In Acton, Christmas comes by fire truck: firefighters bring Santa to the neighborhoods and to Cucurbit Farm, West Acton Village holds a Holiday Stroll, and a local church turns its grounds into Bethlehem.
celebrates: Acton's firefighters are at the heart of the season. Members of Acton Professional Firefighters Local 1904 host Pictures with Santa at Cucurbit Farm, and the Acton Fire Department's Santa Ride carries Santa through the neighborhoods on a vintage fire truck while helpers collect food for the Acton Food Pantry. On the first Saturday of December, the West Acton Village Holiday Stroll invites families to visit local shops and groups, follow a scavenger hunt, meet Santa and finish at a tree lighting. Faith Evangelical Free Church stages Journey to Bethlehem, and the Recreation Department runs holiday craft days.
lastyear: In 2025 the Acton Fire Department's Santa Ride rolled through town on Saturday, December 13, from 9 am to 3 pm. Santa rode a vintage 1936 REO fire truck with a fire department escort and made 18 stops, from Oakwood Road at 9 am to Cucurbit Farm on Parker Street, the Acton Memorial Library lower lot, the NARA Park bathhouse and Alcott Street at Longfellow park at the end of the day. His helpers collected non-perishable food for the Acton Food Pantry along the way.
facts: In Acton, Santa trades his sleigh for a fire truck, and not a new one: the truck that carries him on the Santa Ride is a 1936 REO. The West Acton Village Holiday Stroll has been a community get-together for years. In 2018, 25 organizations took part, with a craft fair at the church, a bake sale for the Acton Food Pantry, a sing-along, a village-wide scavenger hunt with a prize for finishing and a meet and greet with Santa, all wrapped up by a tree lighting at Middlesex Savings Bank.
trains: Acton is on the MBTA Fitchburg Line. South Acton station sits between West Concord and Littleton/Route 495, and trains run east through Concord, Lincoln, Waltham and Porter to North Station in Boston, which makes a holiday trip into the city easy without driving. Closer to home, Lowell has the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society's steam locomotive No. 410 and the National Streetcar Museum, and Edaville in Carver runs a Holiday Express train through acres of Christmas lights.

faq: When is the Acton Santa Ride?

The Acton Fire Department's Santa Ride is held on a Saturday in mid December. In 2025 it ran on December 13 from 9 am to 3 pm, with 18 neighborhood stops including Cucurbit Farm and the Acton Memorial Library lower lot. Santa's helpers collect non-perishable food, so bring a can or box for the Acton Food Pantry.
Where can kids get pictures with Santa in Acton?

Acton Professional Firefighters Local 1904 hosts Pictures with Santa at Cucurbit Farm, 32 Parker Street, in late November. The town posts the details as a news flash, and the firefighters ask families to bring a non-perishable food item. Follow the Acton Fire Santa Ride page for updates.
What is the West Acton Village Holiday Stroll?

It is a community celebration on the first Saturday of December. West Acton businesses and organizations welcome visitors through the day, and families can follow a village-wide scavenger hunt and win a prize for visiting every stop. Past strolls have included a craft fair, a bake sale for the food pantry, Santa and a tree lighting at Middlesex Savings Bank.
Is there a living nativity in Acton?

Yes. Faith Evangelical Free Church at 54 Hosmer Street presents Journey to Bethlehem, a walk-through nativity with indoor and outdoor scenes that takes about an hour. Admission is free, but families reserve a timed entry. The church also offers quieter sensory-friendly journeys for children who need them.

South Acton station on the MBTA Fitchburg Line. Trains run east to North Station in Boston through West Concord, Concord, Lincoln and Waltham, and west to Littleton/Route 495, Ayer and Fitchburg. It gives Acton families a way to reach holiday events in Boston without driving into the city.
